_comment: KNOWN-GAP REPRODUCTION (B) for layout/erc/adc_block.supply-spec.json's
`ties[]` omission. Not an item-11 artifact -- never cite this run as
evidence about this block.
Byte-identical to reproduction A except that the tie carries the
`tap_requires` narrowing klayout-tools#2169 added and docs/cli/erc.md
says to use on gf180mcu: `COMP n Nplus`, i.e. tap_layer 22/0 narrowed
by Nplus 32/0.
EXPECTED OUTCOME: 25 `erc.missing_tie` findings -- one per drawn Nwell
shape in ADC_BLOCK -- and `erc_status: "violations"`.
EVERY ONE OF THOSE FINDINGS IS FALSE. They are produced by the
narrowing intersecting an EMPTY layer: ADC_BLOCK draws no implant
layers anywhere (Nplus 32/0: zero shapes; Pplus 31/0: zero shapes),
because this generated full-custom flow derives implants downstream.
An empty tap region means every well is reported as having no tap
drawn -- which docs/cli/erc.md calls `an honest finding` for a stream
that really draws no taps, and which is simply wrong for one that
draws contacted taps on an undrawn implant.
Taken together, A and B are why the committed supply spec declares NO
`ties[]`: A cannot tell a tap from a source/drain contact, B invents
25 defects, and there is no third form. `run_erc.py` re-runs both and
asserts these outcomes, so the day either stops reproducing -- an
upstream fix, or implants appearing in this block's GDS -- the ERC
flow goes red and the omission gets re-argued instead of inherited.
